title: Mussolini, Feb. 23, 1941: Part 5
topic: Mussolini's February 23, 1941 speech to the Blackshirts of Rome, Part 5 (English translation, radio-style, with dated archival photographs)
caption_extra: Part 5 of Mussolini's February 23, 1941 speech to the Blackshirts of Rome, in English.

beats.narration: It was during October and November that Great Britain gathered and lined up against us the mass of her imperial forces, recruited from three continents and armed by a fourth. She concentrated in Egypt fifteen divisions and a considerable mass of armored means and hurled them against our lines in Marmarica where on the first line were Libyan divisions, brave and faithful but unsuited to bear the attack of enemy machines. On December 9 a battle was thus started, which was only five or ten days in advance of ours, and which brought the enemy to Bengazi.
beats.label: Prisoners, Sidi Barrani, Dec. 1940

beats.narration: We are not like the English. We boast that we are not like them. We haven't elevated lying into a government art nor into a narcotic for the people the way the London government has done. We call bread bread and wine wine, and when the enemy wins a battle it is useless and ridiculous to seek, as the English do in their incomparable hypocrisy, to deny or diminish it.
beats.label: Churchill, Liverpool, April 1941

beats.narration: One entire army, the Tenth, was broken up almost completely with its men and cannon. The Fifth Air Squadron was literally sacrificed, almost entirely. Where possible we resisted strongly and furiously.
beats.label: Prisoners taken at Bardia, 1941

beats.narration: Since we recognize these facts it is useless for the enemy to exaggerate the figures of its booty. It is because we are certain regarding the grade of national maturity reached by the Italian people and regarding the future development of events that we continue to follow the cult of truth and repudiate all falsification.
beats.label: Mussolini in the Chamber, June 1941
